findings.title: Busy times are skipped for every slot inside a date override
findings.body:
`checkIfIsAvailable` returns `true` at lines 133-135 as soon as `dateOverrideExist` is set and the slot was not excluded. That return happens before the `busy.every(...)` check at line 153, so for a fixed host (or a loose host, via the branch at lines 513-518) a slot inside a date override is offered as available even when a calendar event or booking covers it.

Trace: fixed host, date override 14:00-18:00 on day D (`getUserAvailability.ts:215-224` gives start/end as Dates), a Google Calendar event 14:00-15:00 on D. `getSlots` (`packages/lib/slots.ts:112-125`) does not look at busy times, so the 14:00 slot reaches `checkIfIsAvailable` via `slots.ts:488-493`, passes the date-override check, returns `true` at line 134, and is returned to the booker. Before this PR the busy check ran for every slot.

Fix: do not return early. When an override covers the slot, skip only the weekly working-hours check and fall through to `busy.every`.

findings.title: A second date-override row on the same day removes every slot of that day
findings.body:
`dateOverrides.find(...)` returns the first override for which the callback is truthy. The callback returns `true` for any override on the same day that does not contain the slot (lines 117-125). Each slot is therefore checked against each row on its day, and any row that does not contain it excludes it.

Two rows on one date, A 14:00-16:00 and B 18:00-20:00 (IST organizer): the 14:00 slot is inside A but is before B, so B returns `true` and the slot is excluded. The 18:00 slot is inside B but after A, so A returns `true` and it is excluded. The whole day shows no slots. `getUserAvailability.ts:215-224` returns one entry per availability row without merging rows with the same date, so this input reaches the check.

Fix: for the slot's day, take the overrides on that day; exclude the slot only when none of them contains it (`some`, not `find`).

findings.title: Working-hours check removes every slot for a host with two ranges on one weekday
findings.body:
`getWorkingHours` emits one entry per availability row (`packages/lib/availability.ts:92-100`), and `getUserAvailability` returns them unmerged (`packages/core/getUserAvailability.ts:210,229`). The new check at lines 138-148 uses `find` and returns `true` when any same-weekday entry does not contain the slot's start. A host with 09:00-12:00 and 13:00-17:00 on Monday therefore has every Monday slot excluded: 10:00 is inside the first entry, but the second entry makes `find` return `true`.

This applies to all fixed hosts (personal events too, since `isFixed` is true when there is no `schedulingType`, line 369) and to loose hosts (lines 513-518).

Second defect in the same block: `end` (line 142) is computed from `slotStartTime`, not `slotEndTime`, so the upper bound checks only the slot start.

Fix: the containment test must use `some` over the same-day entries, using both slot start and end. Alternatively, drop this block: `getSlots` already limits slots to working hours (`packages/lib/slots.ts:88-90`). Add a test for a split day.

findings.title: Override day selection compares the organizer wall-clock value with invitee-day instants
findings.body:
The filter at lines 206-208 keeps an override when `dayjs.utc(override.start)` falls inside the invitee's day. `override.start` is the organizer's wall-clock time stored as UTC (`getUserAvailability.ts:215-224`, same convention as `getWorkingHours`), not the absolute instant. The PR's new minute conversion (lines 211-225) corrects the time of day, but the day is still chosen with the raw value.

Example: organizer Asia/Kolkata, invitee at UTC+2, override 23:00 IST on day D. The absolute instant is D 17:30Z, which is D 19:30 for the invitee. The invitee's day D window is [D-1 22:00Z, D 22:00Z), and the raw value D 23:00Z is outside it, so the override is dropped from day D. The invitee's day D+1 window includes it, and the minute math produces 19:30 on D+1 (wrong day).

Fix: convert to the absolute instant before the day filter (raw start minus the organizer offset, as in `checkIfIsAvailable`), then filter on that.

findings.title: Override date match uses the server's local timezone while the slot uses UTC
findings.body:
Lines 109-111 format `dayjs(date.start).add(...)` in the process's local timezone and compare it with `slotStartTime.format(...)`, which is UTC (`time.utc()` at line 100). The two agree only when the server runs in UTC. On a server in a negative-offset zone, a shifted override start between 00:00 and about 05:00 UTC formats as the previous day, so the override applies to the wrong UTC day.

Fix: call `.utc()` before `format` on the shifted value. Relevant only if the server is not pinned to UTC.

findings.title: Comparison of two Dayjs objects with === is always false
findings.body: `dayjs(date.start).add(...) === dayjs(date.end).add(...)` compares object identity, so it is always false and the branch at lines 114-116 never runs. It was probably meant to catch zero-length overrides. Compare with `.isSame(...)` or `valueOf()`, or delete the branch and state how zero-length overrides should behave.

findings.title: Date round-trips through toString(); a missing timeZone silently uses the system zone
findings.body:
Lines 212-213 build the value with `dayjs(override.start.toString())`. `Date#toString` drops milliseconds and the parse goes through a locale string. Use `dayjs(override.start)`.

`.tz(override.timeZone)` (line 212) with an undefined `timeZone` falls back to the local zone without an error, so an override that lacks a timezone would be converted with the wrong offset and nothing would report it. Today `getSchedule` always sets `timeZone` (`viewer/slots.ts:413`), and no other caller passes overrides (the team components pass none), so this is latent. Consider making the field required on the override type or guarding it.

findings.title: The @see points at a getWorkingHours signature that no longer exists
findings.body: Line 13 says `getWorkingHours(timeZone: string, availability: Availability[])`. The function in `packages/lib/availability.ts:62-67` takes `relativeTimeUnit: { timeZone?: string; utcOffset?: number }` as its first argument. This was already out of date before the PR, but the PR edits this file and the reference should match.

findings.title: The new test only covers the timezone case; the three regressions are not tested
findings.body: The added assertion (lines 788-804) checks one fixed-host override in Asia/Dhaka. Nothing exercises: busy times on an override day (finding at slots.ts:133), two override rows on the same date (slots.ts:106), or a weekday with two working-hours rows (slots.ts:139). Each of these would have failed in a test. Add one case for each.

contracts.action: Fixed-host check returns true early for a slot that falls inside a date override, so the busy check is never reached for it
contracts.equivalent_path: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/slots.ts:153 (busy.every, run for every slot before this PR)
contracts.before_after: Before: every slot is checked against busy times. After: on an override day, a slot inside the override returns true at 133-135 before busy.every at 153.
contracts.visible_effect: Booked or calendar-busy slots on a date-override day are offered to the booker.
contracts.failure_mode: Double booking on override days. Nothing reports it; the slot is simply shown as free.

contracts.action: New per-host working-hours containment check inside checkIfIsAvailable
contracts.equivalent_path: packages/lib/slots.ts:88-90 (getSlots already limits slots to working hours); packages/core/getAggregateWorkingHours.ts:19 (personal events flatMap the working hours)
contracts.before_after: Before: no per-host working-hours check in checkIfIsAvailable. After: find() excludes a slot if any same-weekday entry does not contain it.
contracts.visible_effect: A host whose weekday has two ranges (split day) gets no slots at all for that weekday.
contracts.failure_mode: Silent. The booker sees no times and no error is produced.

contracts.action: Date override rows are flattened with a per-user timeZone and passed to getTimeSlots; checkIfIsAvailable receives the host's own timeZone as organizerTimeZone
contracts.before_after: Before: overrides had no timeZone and a single event-level organizerTimeZone was used. After: each override carries its user's timeZone and each host's check uses its own.
contracts.visible_effect: None directly; the conversion depends on the timezone being set.
contracts.failure_mode: If timeZone is undefined, the conversion silently uses the system zone (lib/slots.ts:212).
contracts.open_question: Can availability.timeZone be null or undefined for a user, and does getUserAvailability's fallback (schedule, then eventType, then user) always produce a value?

contracts.action: Date override minutes are now converted from organizer to invitee local time before buildSlots
contracts.equivalent_path: packages/lib/slots.ts:107-110 (getTime turns invitee-local minutes into an instant)
contracts.before_after: Before: override minutes were UTC minute-of-day, which is only correct for a UTC invitee. After: minutes are offset by (invitee offset minus organizer offset) at override.start.
contracts.visible_effect: Date-override slots appear at the correct time for a non-UTC invitee (the Dhaka assertion in the new test).
contracts.failure_mode: Day selection is not converted (see the separate finding at lib/slots.ts:207), so an override near midnight can be dropped or shown on the wrong day.

contracts.action: Day filter for date overrides in getSlots, unchanged but now feeding the converted minutes
contracts.equivalent_path: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/slots.ts:105-107 (checkIfIsAvailable converts the override to an absolute instant before matching the day)
contracts.before_after: Unchanged. The filter uses the raw organizer wall-clock value against invitee-day instants, while checkIfIsAvailable converts first.
contracts.visible_effect: An override whose absolute time falls on a different invitee day can be dropped from its day or shown on the next day.
contracts.failure_mode: Silent wrong availability on the affected day.

contracts.action: Reserved-slot busy branch calls checkIfIsAvailable with busy but without dateOverrides or workingHours
contracts.equivalent_path: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/slots.ts:513-518 (loose-host branch, which passes the full userSchedule)
contracts.before_after: Before: no date-override or working-hours check here. After: only organizerTimeZone is added, and the new checks default to empty so they are skipped.

summary: The Dhaka assertion in the new test appears to pass when traced by hand (I did not run it). The override minute conversion in packages/lib/slots.ts is correct for the case it targets. The change to checkIfIsAvailable in packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/slots.ts introduces three blocker regressions: busy times are skipped on override days (line 133), a second override row on the same date removes all of that day's slots (line 106), and a split weekday removes all slots for that host (line 139). None of these is covered by the test. Also flagged: a day-selection mismatch in lib/slots.ts (line 207, fix), a server-local-timezone date match (consider), a dead Dayjs identity comparison (consider), and a stale @see in schedule.d.ts (consider). The base commit has no CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md or docs/adr entries, so no repository rules were applied. The changed code is server-side tRPC and has no UI state, so the remount, Back and window-default items do not apply.
